title: Grateful Dead Live at Seattle Center Arena on 1973-06-26

ai_review.summary: A patchy matrix recording with occasional dropouts captures a lively 1973 Seattle show featuring standout renditions of "You Ain't Woman Enough", "China Cat Sunflower" and an epic "Truckin' > Drums > The Other One" sequence.
ai_review.review: The performance is energetic and full of classic ’73 moments – rare vocal showcases on "You Ain't Woman Enough", a scorching Bob Weir on China Cat, and a seamless Truckin’‑Drums‑Other One sandwich that many reviewers call magical.  Technically the tape jumps between soundboard and audience sources, with noticeable stitching, brief drop‑outs and channel switches that can pull you out of the music, though several listeners still find it listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (several 5‑star comments) while noting consistent recording issues; weighting show quality higher yields an overall rating just above four stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stitched together from soundboard and audience patches, causing audible jumps; brief drop‑outs (e.g., Truckin'), channel swaps and pitch inconsistencies are mentioned. Overall clarity varies but the mix is still usable.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > Riding on the Clouds
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set is solid with a few slower moments, while the second set builds momentum and delivers strong segues—especially the Truckin' sandwich. Recording patches interrupt flow in places but the musical arc remains engaging.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Generally solid lead guitar work; some reviewers note he fades during China Cat Sunflower.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass praised as a ‘monster’ on several tracks (Bertha, He's Gone, The Other One).
band_member_comments.Bob: Highly lauded rhythm‑guitar performance, especially on China Cat Sunflower where he 'annihilates' the part.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's intros are highlighted as great; occasional kludgey moments noted but overall positive.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming shines in the Truckin' > Drums > The Other One sequence, receiving strong commendation.
